get.description:
Returns a paginated list of bookings for the account. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number. Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters.

Filtering, sorting and field selection are supported via query parameters:

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>][<operator>]` | Filter by a field, e.g. `filter[client_id][equal]=2`. |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`. |
| `fields[]` | Restrict the returned columns. |
| `search` | Free-text search. |

The response is a standard paginated envelope; each item in `data` is a booking record.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Items per page. Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

data.description: The bookings on this page. Each item is a booking record (its fields depend on the account's booking configuration — e.g. id, no, date, start/end time, client, staff, status, and totals).

payment_status.description: Booking status code (0 Pending, 1 Confirmed, 2 Invoiced, 3 Cancelled, 4 Done).

400.description: The list could not be produced — for example the booking entity is unavailable for this account or the required plugin is inactive.

error.description: Reason the request failed (e.g. the booking entity is not available for the account, or the required plugin is not active).

401.description: The authenticated user lacks permission to view bookings.

error.example: You are not allowed to view this page

get.description:
Returns a single booking by id. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page or format flag.

The successful response is a **flat object** of the booking's fields (it is not wrapped in a `data` envelope) and may include related records and a `custom_data` object.

Note: requesting an id that does not exist currently returns HTTP 500 with the plain-text body `error happened` rather than a 404.

parameters.name: bookingId
parameters.description: The id of the booking to fetch.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

200.description: The booking record (flat object, plus any related records and custom_data).

schema.description: A single booking record, returned flat (not wrapped). Fields depend on the account's booking configuration.

payment_status.description: Booking status code (0 Pending, 1 Confirmed, 2 Invoiced, 3 Cancelled, 4 Done).

custom_data.description: Custom-field values for the booking, when present.

401.description: The authenticated user lacks permission to view bookings.

error.example: You are not allowed to view this page

500.description: Returned as plain text `error happened` when the record cannot be fetched — including when the id does not exist (a not-found case is not surfaced as 404).

post.description:
Creates a new booking (an appointment-style record). Provide the client, the booking date, and one or more services to book.

Each entry in `InvoiceItem` must reference an **active bookable service** — a product of type *Service* that has a duration configured and belongs to at least one category. A request whose services are not valid bookable services is rejected with `Please Enter Valid Service`.

The end time is calculated automatically from the services' durations, and the booking's staff and status are assigned automatically — you do not send them. Set `Invoice.convert` to `1` to immediately convert the new booking into an invoice within the same request; the response then also returns `invoice_id`.

The `.json` extension is optional and does not change the response.

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

client_id.description: Required. The id of an existing client the booking is for.

date.description: Required. The booking date in `dd/mm/yyyy` format.

start_time.description: Optional. Start time in 24-hour `HH:mm` format. Defaults to the start of the day when omitted.

description.description: Optional. Free-text note stored on the booking.

branch_id.description: Optional. The branch the booking belongs to. Defaults to the request's current branch.

convert.description: Optional. Set to `1` to also convert the created booking into an invoice in the same request; the response then includes `invoice_id`. Defaults to `0`.

InvoiceItem.description: The services to book. At least one is required and each must reference an active bookable service product.

product_id.description: Required. The id of a bookable service product (type *Service*, with a duration and a category).

200.description: The booking was created. Note this endpoint returns a `{code, message, id, appointment_id}` object (not the standard result envelope). When `Invoice.convert` was `1`, `invoice_id` is also returned; if the conversion failed, an `error` message is returned instead of `invoice_id`.

id.description: The id of the created booking.

appointment_id.description: The id of the appointment created for the booking.

invoice_id.description: Only present when `Invoice.convert` was `1` and conversion succeeded — the id of the invoice created from the booking.

400.description: The booking could not be created. Two cases: an invalid bookable service returns `{ code: 400, errors: "Please Enter Valid Service" }`; a save failure returns `{ code: 400, message: ... }`.

errors.description: Present when a booked service is not a valid bookable service.

message.description: Present when the booking itself could not be saved.

delete.description:
Deletes a booking by its id. A booking can only be deleted when you have permission and it has **not** already been converted to an invoice — otherwise the request is rejected. Deleting a booking also removes its linked appointment.

The `.json` extension is optional.

parameters.name: bookingId
parameters.description: The id of the booking to delete.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

400.description: The booking could not be deleted — you lack permission, or it has already been converted to an invoice.

message.example: Booking#00002 Delete Failed, Please Make Sure You Have the Permission And the Booking is Not Converted to Invoice

404.description: No booking exists with the given id.

get.description:
Changes the status of a booking. Pass the booking id and the target status code in the path.

| Value | Status |
|---|---|
| 0 | Pending |
| 1 | Confirmed |
| 2 | Invoiced (set automatically when the booking is converted to an invoice) |
| 3 | Cancelled |
| 4 | Done |

Typically you set `1` (Confirmed), `3` (Cancelled), or `4` (Done). The request always responds with HTTP 200 carrying an `error` flag: `error` is `false` when the status was changed, and `true` when it was not (for example an unsupported status, or a booking already converted to an invoice). A booking id that does not exist returns 404.

The `.json` extension is optional.

parameters.name: bookingId
parameters.description: The id of the booking whose status is being changed.

parameters.name: bookingStatus
parameters.description: Target status code. `0` Pending · `1` Confirmed · `2` Invoiced · `3` Cancelled · `4` Done.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

200.description: Always returned (HTTP 200) whether or not the change applied — check the `error` flag. Success: `{"message":"Status Changed Successfully","error":false}`. Not applied: `{"message":"","error":true}`.

message.description: Result message. Empty when the change was not applied.

error.description: `false` when the status was changed; `true` when it was not applied (unsupported status, or booking already converted).

404.description: No booking exists with the given id.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of work orders for the authenticated account.

Requires the `View his work orders` or `View all work orders` permission. Staff who only hold `View his work orders` see only the work orders they created or are assigned to. Workflow-type entities are excluded — only classic work orders are returned.

**Default status filter:** when no `status` filter is supplied, the list returns only **Open** work orders. Pass `status=-1` to return every status, or a specific status value to filter.

Each item is returned under a `WorkOrder` key; related records (client, staff, follow-up status) are not embedded.

Filter by work order status. When omitted, only Open work orders are returned. Pass `-1` to return all statuses.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Open |
| 2 | Closed |
| 3 | Cancelled |
| 4 | Draft |
| -1 | All statuses |

post.description:
Creates a new work order.

Requires the `Add new work orders` permission. The request body must be wrapped in a `WorkOrder` object. Only `title` is required.

Several fields are set automatically and cannot be controlled by the caller: the work order `number` is generated when omitted, `start_date` defaults to today when omitted, the creator is recorded as the authenticated user, and `status` is set to Open (or Draft when `is_draft` is sent). On success the new work order id is returned with HTTP 202.

put.description:
Updates an existing work order.

Requires permission to edit the work order (`Edit & remove all work orders`, or `Edit & remove his work orders` for one the staff created or is assigned to). The request body must be wrapped in a `WorkOrder` object; `title` and `start_date` are required.

A **Closed** work order cannot be edited and returns `400`. As with create, `status` is server-controlled (Open, or Draft when `is_draft` is sent), `number` is generated when omitted, and the submitted `staff_id` assigns staff member(s) rather than changing the creator. The same operation is also reachable via `POST /work_orders/{id}`.

delete.description:
Deletes a work order by its identifier.

Requires permission to edit/remove the work order, and the work order must have no blocking related transactions (invoices, credit notes, refunds, expenses, requisitions, purchase orders, etc.) — otherwise the request is rejected with `403`. Its start date must not fall within a closed financial period.

For API callers the deletion is confirmed automatically (no confirmation step). On success the deleted-confirmation message is returned with HTTP 200.

message.example: Item was not deleted. If you see this again, please contact customer support.

post.description: Updates an existing work-order appointment. Send only the fields to change, wrapped in a `WorkOrderAppointment` object; omitted fields keep their current values. Requires permission to edit appointments/notes. Requires the Work Orders plugin to be enabled. This `POST` route is an alias of the `PUT` update endpoint for the same path.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The work-order appointment's identifier.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

item_id.description: The work order id to attach the appointment to.

date.description: Appointment start date/time. Must be earlier than `end_date`.

end_date.description: Appointment end date/time. Optional; computed from `duration` when omitted.

duration.description: Appointment length in hours (numeric) or as `HH:MM`. Optional; defaults to 1 hour and is used to compute `end_date` when `end_date` is not supplied.

staff_id.description: Id of the creating staff member, or an array of staff ids to assign. Defaults to the authenticated staff when omitted.

status.description:
Appointment status.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Scheduled |
| 1 | Done |
| 2 | Dismissed |

recurring.description: Set to `1` to create a repeating appointment; supply the recurrence in the `RecurringAppointment` object.

share_with_partner.description: Share the appointment with the linked partner (the work order's client).

period_unit.description: Repeat interval (number of `unit_name` units between occurrences).

400.description: Validation failed; `validation_errors` lists the offending fields.

403.description: The caller lacks permission for this operation.

404.description: No work-order appointment matches the supplied id.
